original_paragraph: The International Safety Management (ISM) Code is mandatory for yachts of 500 gross tonnage and above that are engaged in trade, which in practice means charter. It requires a documented Safety Management System, a Document of Compliance held by the managing company, and regular audit. A privately used yacht is outside the mandatory regime whatever its size, although an owner can adopt ISM voluntarily, and some flags, Malta among them, offer voluntary certification. Yachts engaged in commercial operation also fall under the Maritime Labour Convention (MLC), which governs crew working conditions, contracts, hours, and welfare. Where they apply, both frameworks are binding and audited. Amendments to the Maritime Labour Convention in force since December 2024 require reasonable-cost internet access, free food and drinking water, and protective equipment in suitable sizes. Further amendments are expected to enter into force on 23 December 2027: they strengthen shore leave, define what repatriation must cover, and require measures against violence and harassment on board. For a charter yacht that means revised crew agreements and complaint procedures during 2027, normally handled by the management company.

original_paragraph: Cover for sexual misconduct claims is a newer question. In a 2025 case, a crewmember who was sexually assaulted in English Harbour, Antigua, aboard a St Vincent-flagged yacht owned through a Marshall Islands LLC, had the vessel arrested at its Fort Lauderdale berth on a US maritime lien after the local authorities did not act. The case raises three points. Yacht liability policies routinely exclude sexual misconduct claims; where the exclusion is enforceable, the owner is personally liable for the claim and the defence. The maritime lien attaches at injury, travels with the vessel and is exposed the first time the vessel enters a US port; a foreign flag and an offshore SPV do not defeat an in rem arrest under 28 U.S.C. § 1333. US policies also contain strict notice provisions, and delay or concealment of an allegation can affect coverage. Supplemental sexual misconduct cover is available, some owners now buy it, and it is arranged with the broker before an incident, not after (Adria Notari and Ryan Melogy, plaintiff’s US maritime counsel, in The Superyacht Report, Q2 2026).

original_paragraph: EU ETS Maritime is the best known, and it reaches fewer yachts than is often assumed. In force from 1 January 2024, it applies to ships of 5,000 GT and above that carry passengers or cargo for commercial purposes to or from EEA ports. Compliance is phased by emissions year: 40 percent of 2024 emissions (surrendered in 2025), 70 percent of 2025 emissions, and 100 percent of 2026 emissions onward, first due by 30 September 2027. A yacht in private use sits outside the system at any size. A yacht of 5,000 GT or more on commercial charter can fall inside it, and published guidance does not settle the position of charter yachts certified for 12 passengers or fewer. The strategy shapes the commercial shipping fuel transition that reaches yachting through fuel availability and cost. The IMO Net-Zero Framework, which would add a global fuel standard and emissions pricing for ships of 5,000 GT and above in international shipping, was approved in April 2025; a vote to adopt it was adjourned in October 2025 and resumes on 4 December 2026. original_paragraph: The nearest practical answer is hydrotreated vegetable oil. HVO is a paraffinic diesel made from waste fats and vegetable oils and a drop-in replacement for marine gas oil: engines approved for paraffinic fuel run on it, usually without change to fuel systems or tanks, and the engine maker’s approval should be confirmed. original_paragraph: Two developments in 2026 bear on how the holding structure is built. On 21 May 2026 the Court of Justice of the European Union held, in joined Cases C-428/24 and C-476/24 concerning Sailing Yacht A, that assets held in a trust can be treated under EU sanctions law as owned or controlled by a sanctioned beneficiary, and that terms in the trust deed do not of themselves prevent a freeze. The case has returned to the Italian courts and the yacht remains seized. A trust above the yacht’s holding company is a succession arrangement; it does not place the yacht beyond measures aimed at the person who benefits from it. Separately, Switzerland opened a federal register of beneficial owners on 1 October 2026. It is not public, but a Swiss company, or a foreign holding company whose decisions are in practice taken in Switzerland, must file the natural persons who control it, with changes reported within a month. From the same date, Swiss lawyers, fiduciaries and multi-family offices that set up or fund a company abroad for a client carry anti-money-laundering due diligence, including questions on the source of funds where the risk warrants it.
